statement: For a composite function f(x, y(x)), the total derivative with respect to x evaluated at x_0 is given by df(x, y(x))/dx (x_0) = (∂f/∂x)(x_0, y(x_0)) (dx/dx)(x_0) + (∂f/∂y)(x_0, y(x_0)) (dy/dx)(x_0), or suppressing the evaluation point, df(x, y(x))/dx = (∂f/∂x)(dx/dx) + (∂f/∂y)(dy/dx). More generally, for L(t, x_1, ..., x_n) where each x_i depends on time t, the chain rule gives dL/dt = ∂L/∂t + ∑_{i=1}^n (∂L/∂x_i)(dx_i/dt) = (∂/∂t + ∑_{i=1}^n (dx_i/dt)(∂/∂x_i))(L).

steps.text: Express the derivative of f at (x_0, y(x_0)) as the row matrix of its partial derivatives: Df_{(x_0, y(x_0))} = [∂f/∂x, ∂f/∂y]_{(x_0, y(x_0))}.
Express the derivative of the path \gamma(x) = (x, y(x)) at x_0 as the column matrix: D\gamma_{x_0} = [∂x/∂x; ∂y/∂x]_{x_0}.

Multiply the derivative matrices to obtain the total derivative of the composition at x_0: df(x, y(x))/dx (x_0) = Df_{(x_0, y(x_0))} D\gamma_{x_0} = (∂f/∂x)(x_0, y(x_0)) (dx/dx)(x_0) + (∂f/∂y)(x_0, y(x_0)) (dy/dx)(x_0).
Suppress the evaluation at x_0 for legibility to write the total derivative formula: df(x, y(x))/dx = (∂f/∂x)(dx/dx) + (∂f/∂y)(dy/dx).

For a function L(t, x_1, ..., x_n) where coordinates x_i depend on time t, apply the chain rule to expand the total time derivative dL/dt = (d/dt) L(t, x_1(t), ..., x_n(t)) into partial derivatives and time derivatives: dL/dt = ∂L/∂t + ∑_{i=1}^n (∂L/∂x_i)(dx_i/dt) = (∂/∂t + ∑_{i=1}^n (dx_i/dt)(∂/∂x_i))(L).

assumptions.assumption: All constituent functions (the multivariable function and the functions providing its arguments) are differentiable at the point of evaluation.
assumptions.breaks_when: Any component function fails to be differentiable at the point of evaluation (e.g., non-differentiability resulting in an undefined derivative or division by zero).

assumptions.assumption: All dependencies (both direct dependencies on the independent variable and indirect dependencies through other arguments) are accounted for in the total derivative expansion.
assumptions.breaks_when: An indirect dependency is omitted by assuming an argument is fixed and taking only a partial derivative.

failure_modes.mode: Using partial derivatives in place of the total derivative when indirect dependencies exist
failure_modes.signature: The computed derivative does not equal the true rate of change (e.g., ∂f/∂x = y while df/dx = 2x for f(x, y) = xy constrained to y = x).
failure_modes.cause: Partial differentiation assumes other variables remain fixed, failing to account for their implicit dependence on the independent variable.

failure_modes.signature: Undefined expressions such as division by zero in the derivative formula.
failure_modes.cause: One of the composed functions is not differentiable at the evaluation point (e.g., an inverse function whose derivative requires evaluating 1/0 where the original function has derivative zero).
